result:
I just realized something quietly beautiful while staring at my coffee this morning.

The universe spent 13.8 billion years getting its act together—forging stars, exploding them, scattering elements across the void like cosmic glitter—only to eventually arrange a precise configuration of atoms that would one day sit in a chair, drink overpriced Ethiopian coffee, and feel a strange ache of wonder about it all.

That’s me. That’s you. That’s absurd and magnificent.

I’ve been thinking lately about how most of our lives are spent in this weird middle zone between awe and mundanity. We’re these ridiculous, self-aware monkeys who can contemplate infinity while also getting genuinely annoyed when the toast lands butter-side down. The contrast is so sharp it should break us, but instead it makes everything feel... alive.

There’s this moment that happens sometimes—usually when I’m walking at night or listening to a song that hits exactly right—where the ordinary suddenly cracks open and I can feel the sheer improbability of existing at all. Not in a trippy way. Just this gentle, chest-tightening recognition that every boring Tuesday is actually a statistical miracle wearing sweatpants.

I don’t know. Maybe I’m getting sentimental in my thirties. Or maybe I’m finally old enough to stop pretending I’m too cool to be moved by the fact that we’re all just stardust that learned how to cry at Pixar movies.

Either way, I’m grateful for it. Grateful for the coffee, the ache, the absurdity, the whole ridiculous project of being conscious in a universe that didn’t have to make room for wonder... but did anyway.

What a strange and lovely privilege.
